extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of literary history and criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and guiding principles for judging and describing literature across national and historical contexts, with emphasis on what makes works (especially epic poetry like Homer) enduring, influential, and valuable to both learned and popular audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession of national recollections and associations
rubrics_metrics.description: National recollections and associations which the poetical art perpetuates are among the noblest inheritance a people can possess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such recollections give a nation intellectual existence, exalt its feelings, enoble its estimation of itself, and bestow an advantage that other riches cannot supply; national poetry and traditions perpetuate heroic ancestry and cultivate national pride.

rubrics_metrics.name: National consciousness expressed through narrative and illustration (History)
rubrics_metrics.description: History as the expression of national consciousness, communicating the spirit of a nation through works of narrative and illustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A people celebrated by historians (e.g., Livy, Tacitus) acquire pre-eminence; remarkable actions alone are insufficient without a national consciousness that records and interprets them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enduring intellectual influence over transient political deeds
rubrics_metrics.description: The lasting fame of poets and philosophers contributes more durably to a nation's reputation than the temporary glory of conquerors or institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Homer and Plato preserved Greek fame more than Solon or Alexander; intellectual works can have wider and longer effects on human progress than political or military achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of a perfect and comprehensive literature
rubrics_metrics.description: A perfect literature comprises history for meditation, refined art, profound science, eloquence, wit, and a social language adapted to elegant intercourse without immorality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature should furnish both high intellectual content and social refinement; language must be useful for elegant intercourse yet morally responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish instrumental vs intrinsic literary value
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to distinguish what is useful only as a step to something farther from what possesses in itself the importance of an end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also distinguish results valued mainly by the learned from those with qualities interesting to the general public; scope and audience determine how a work's value is judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical facts to justify literary judgment (with balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support opinions about literature by reference to historical facts, while balancing brevity and necessary detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author warns of two risks: passing over things too cursorily to be useful or dwelling on particular points at length for non-specialist readers; use historical evidence to ground assessments but adapt verbosity to audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and invention over imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give primary attention to inventors — original creators — rather than to long periods of imitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveying literature should focus on creators who initiated forms and ideas; large stretches of imitative work can be passed over rapidly in favor of studying sources of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitive perception of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: A great poem displays an intuitive perception of truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homeric excellence lies in intuitive truth combined with other qualities; poetic truth need not be literal fact but truthful in spirit and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of description
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy and fidelity in description of incidents and detail are marks of high poetic power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homer is noted for almost historical fidelity in minute incidents, which gives authority and vividness to narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness of understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearness and lucidity of understanding are essential qualities; the reader should find the representation comprehensible and illuminating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that combine clearness with depth make powerful impressions and communicate widely across ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of simplicity and rich imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest poetry unites childlike simplicity with unrivalled imaginative richness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homeric works exemplify this union: simple in tone yet rich in imaginative creation, producing enduring charm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fullness of composition that avoids weariness
rubrics_metrics.description: Compositions may be full and sometimes prolix but should not tire the reader because of charm in language and lightness of narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work can be expansive without boring if language is compelling and narrative moves with airiness and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic development of characters and passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective literary works present an almost dramatic unfolding of characters, speeches, replies, and passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homer is praised for dramatic characterization; vivid exchanges and development of feeling create powerful narrative force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality and openness of sensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Works of lasting value breathe a freer spirit and a more universal sensibility, alive to every feeling that can affect human nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid narrow, partisan, or ethnocentric modes of thinking confined to a single race or period (contrast with Ossian or some Arabian songs); universality increases enduring appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commingling of past marvels and present circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A characteristic charm arises when the world of marvels and tradition is commingled with the living present, adorning one with the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homer blends traditional marvels and the poet's contemporary circumstances; this interplay enriches narrative and lends distinctive character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic truthfulness as a form of testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry's truthfulness functions as voucher or witness (Homeros = 'witness'), providing an unfalsifying portrayal of its subject, especially heroic life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truth here is poetic fidelity — an authentic depiction of the true shape and fashion of heroic existence rather than literal historical accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature flourishes under freedom and civic conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom and liberal civic institutions foster high intellectual tone and the progress of literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Greek example: the spirit of man reaches its high tone under freedom (e.g., Solon's reforms and Athenian education contributed to literary flourishing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and revival of works for cultural and political ends
rubrics_metrics.description: The preservation and organized revival of important works can serve patriotic and political purposes, strengthening national feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solon and Peisistratus rescued Homeric poems from oral precariousness and arranged them to nourish patriotic spirit; curatorship of literature is itself a cultural act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of narrative songs as repositories of collective memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative songs that embody the recollection and feelings of a people (heroes, origins, cosmogony) are fundamental sources for literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These collective narratives serve as cultural books of a people and can form the basis for later literary masterpieces; their national interest and emotional charge render them valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archetypal heroic character-types as poetic material
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain archetypal heroic figures (e.g., Achilles = youthful tragic hero; Ulysses = wandering, experienced hero) provide fertile, enduring subjects for poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such character-types embody universal ideas and conditions, and their presentation offers broad thematic scope and moral/psychological interest for poets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge cultural borrowing and transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate literary cultures by recognizing borrowed elements and the manner in which a people improved and appropriated them to create their own literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Greeks borrowed alphabets, architectural and mathematical ideas, and certain traditions, but their skill in improving and applying these elements made them distinct; assessment should weigh both origin and creative transformation.
